confirmed_decisions: Litera is a self-hosted digital book library/server.
TypeScript, Vue.js, npm, Docker and Docker Compose are the implementation direction.
The proprietary reader experience is the primary product differentiator.
EPUB and PDF are first-class MVP formats.
Metadata is extracted and enriched through external provider integrations.
The UI is editorial, elegant and responsive.
A dedicated /legacy client must preserve core reading flows for an older physical iPad in the iOS 10.x / old WebKit generation; exact device/version remains to be confirmed.
Progressive enhancement/fallback must be automatic rather than a manual mode choice.
The /legacy client is a separate conservative frontend over the same Litera API and can be enabled/disabled by an administrator.
inferred_decisions: The backend should expose a versionable API suitable for a future mobile client.
Reading progress is private user data and should be protected by server-side authorization.
A provider adapter boundary is preferable to hard-coding one metadata source.
engineering_defaults: Use PostgreSQL for the normal multi-user deployment unless implementation evidence favors another choice.
Use local authentication in the initial implementation.
Keep offline-first functionality out of MVP while preserving future compatibility.
open_questions: Final metadata provider set and licensing/API limits should be verified against current official documentation before implementation.
Exact EPUB and PDF rendering engines should be selected after compatibility/security evaluation.
The exact browser compatibility floor should be validated on the physical iOS 10.x reference iPad and representative old Android hardware.
